description: Sabotages for rc-errors. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: The two orderings on the shared error's last drop -- the decrement's Release and the Acquire fence after it -- are recorded below as surviving: weakening either is a real defect, a data race between the last reader of the error and its destruction, but no test can make it fail on a strongly ordered machine, and on a weakly ordered one only by chance (RCE-D-8). They are entries so that a sweep keeps saying so. Undefined behaviour inside the unsafe blocks that shows as no wrong pointer, layout or count is what Miri would add, parked as RCE-inf.1. Global's free of a zero-sized block is not sabotaged: making it free one would hand the global allocator a dangling pointer, which crashes rather than failing a test.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.2: the block is freed while a reference remains
sabotages.why: Freeing when the count reaches one instead of zero frees the block under the last reference, which then reads freed memory. The recording allocator's counts see the free happen while a clone is still alive.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.2: a clone does not count itself
sabotages.why: A clone that does not increment lets the first drop free the block under every other reference.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.2: the block is freed with the error's layout
sabotages.why: The allocator must be given back the layout it allocated, which is the whole block's; the error's alone is smaller. The recording allocator refuses a free whose layout differs.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.2: the error is never dropped
sabotages.why: Freeing the block without dropping the error leaks whatever the error owns. The tests' errors count their drops.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.2: the last decrement does not release
sabotages.why: A real defect that no test can see: without Release, another thread's use of the error is not ordered before the last reference destroys it. On a strongly ordered machine the hardware orders it anyway, so the suite passes (RCE-D-8).

sabotages.name: RCE-1.2: the last drop does not acquire
sabotages.why: A real defect that no test can see: without the Acquire fence, the destruction is not ordered after every other reference's use of the error. As for the decrement, a strongly ordered machine hides it (RCE-D-8).

sabotages.name: RCE-1.2: a clone counts with a stronger ordering than it needs
sabotages.why: The control. A clone is made from a reference already held, so Relaxed is enough; SeqCst is slower and not wrong. A test that failed here would be asserting the implementation.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.3: a shared report derefs to the SharedError and not to its error
sabotages.why: The defect RCE-1.3 found before commit: a SharedError is an Error itself, so handing it out coerces the wrapper, and downcasting sees the wrapper and not the error a caller made.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.3: reports of different forms are equal
sabotages.why: A static report and a shared one are different errors, even with the same message.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.3: static reports are all equal
sabotages.why: Identity of a static report is the static's address; two statics with the same message are still two errors.

sabotages.name: RCE-1.1: a zero-sized block is not aligned
sabotages.why: A zero-sized block must still be aligned to its layout; an address of one is aligned only to one.
